day_shape: Strait of Hormuz dominates: four-way Amman FMs meeting (Saudi/Turkey/Egypt/Pakistan), CENTCOM reports 48 vessels redirected under Iran blockade, Rubio-Miliband reaffirm transit commitment; two IDF reservists killed in south Lebanon IED, IDF resumes precise strikes; UN says Iran executed 56 since March.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz diplomacy and blockade
threads.summary: Foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Egypt and Pakistan met in Amman to discuss Hormuz security and referenced the 18 June Iran-US memorandum, while Rubio and UK Foreign Secretary Miliband reaffirmed commitment to safe transit. CENTCOM said as of 5 August its forces had redirected 48 commercial vessels, disabled 2 and boarded 2 enforcing the blockade; Iran International reported Tehran-Oman talks would require coordination with Iran even from the Omani side.

threads.label: Iraq oil-export fallout from Hormuz closure
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported many Iraqi public employees had not received their July salaries as the prolonged Hormuz disruption squeezed oil exports. Iran International reported a state-owned Iranian bank froze National Iranian Oil Company accounts over unpaid debts, per Fars.

threads.label: South Lebanon strikes and IDF casualties
threads.summary: The IDF announced two reservists — Maj. Harel Birenstock and Sgt. Maj. Tamir Vaknin of the 55th Paratroopers Brigade — were killed and four seriously wounded by an IED in Majdal Zoun, and launched precise strikes across southern Lebanon after an evacuation warning for Mansouri. Lebanese media reported one dead and 11 wounded in a strike on a prayer room in Tebnine; PM Nawaf Salam accused Hezbollah of dragging Lebanon into war as US-backed disarmament talks continued.

threads.label: Israeli activists cross Lebanon border
threads.summary: The IDF said roughly 15-17 Uri Tzafon settlement activists illegally crossed into Lebanon near Ghajar, damaging the border fence before being located and returned by troops. All were handed to police for questioning.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressures and rights
threads.summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk said Iran had executed at least 56 people on national security charges since 19 March, including 27 linked to earlier protests, while Iran International reported nurses were assaulted and dismissed after striking in Tehran and covered a national energy crisis. ReliefWeb published an OCHA update describing a nationwide complex emergency across 30 of 31 provinces following the 28 February escalation.

threads.label: Tehran leadership messaging
threads.summary: President Pezeshkian said in a state TV interview that Iran was being managed with strength despite enemy plans, while telling Jerusalem Post that interaction with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is 'very difficult'. Khamenei's office issued a message urging unity and warning against political discord; Iran International reported parliament has faded further from power toward the IRGC.

threads.label: Regime messaging on US and Al-Udeid
threads.summary: IRIB aired remarks from air force deputy commander Amir Sartip Jafari claiming Su-24 pilots pushed through heavy US air defences at Al-Udeid, and army spokesman Akrami-Nia said Iran's army was fully ready with renewed equipment. MP Morteza Mahmoudi claimed on IRIB that US aims had been reduced to reopening the Strait of Hormuz; Treasury separately removed an IRGC-linked airline from the sanctions list while stating no policy change.

events.title: Defense Minister Israel Katz says he has instructed the army not carry out a planned reduction in the number of active duty reservists in the Gaza border communities' civil defense squads. The IDF has sought to release from reserve duty members of local security teams on all fronts, as their service is superfluous and costly. The military has two divisions operating in Gaza, and the civil defense squads in the border communities remain armed even outside of active reserve duty. Katz says the IDF will not carry out any further reduction in forces until decided otherwise, "in order to preserve the resident's sense of security."
